name: Percy Davila
life: “I still remember getting my first trim after I moved into a rented room.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Percy by a small Monday habit. Percy can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I used the free offer as an excuse to get out of my room after my husband left.
appearance: Percy is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf, Percy holds eye contact until the other person has finished when listening.
personality: Percy keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Percy wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To get a morning outside the empty room.
family: Philip Meyer is Percy’s half-sibling. Percy brings a spare shopping bag. Philip chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A summer marriage*, Philip says, “I offered to officiate because I could do the ceremony in both their languages.”
connections: Chris Valdez (barber). A free fringe buys the customer and the barber a perfectly real conversation.

reactions.situation: A customer uses the free haircut to talk
reactions.response: Percy lets the visitor say whether they would like a trim as well as a talk.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Percy offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.
